title: Jump to the agent that has waited longest for you (needs-you queue)
body:
Add a leader command that jumps to the agent pane that has waited longest in "needs you" state, across all projects. Builds on the shipped agent state (docs/agent-state.md); no new state detection.

DESIGN (decided; if you find it wrong, `kanban block` with the reason rather than switching silently):
- A FIFO queue on the desktop of (project tag, terminal tag) pairs, the same pair a hook event carries (terminal ids repeat across projects). No timestamps: arrival order is wait order.
- Maintain it at the single hook choke point: src/main.rs, `self.desktop.apply_hook_event(&event)`. After the event applies: PermissionRequest -> push to the back unless already queued (Grok replays Claude's hooks, so duplicates arrive). Any event that moves the pane out of NeedsYou (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse while NeedsYou, Stop, StopFailure, Interrupt; see AgentStateSlot::apply in src/agent_state.rs) -> remove it. Only change the queue when apply_hook_event returned true (it drops provider/icon mismatches).
- Exits that send no event (pane closed, process exited, agent quit to its shell so the badge is None, the badges setting toggled -> reset_agent_state) are handled lazily: on the keypress, pop from the front while the entry is not a live pane whose badge is NeedsYou, then jump to the first live one.
- Jumping does NOT dequeue: the pane stays at the front until the human actually answers (the leave event removes it). Pressing the key again with nothing answered lands on the same pane.
- Jump = surface + focus via the existing `WindowManager::surface_target(TargetPath)` (src/wm.rs; it restores minimized windows, switches tabs, clears zooms, runs the focus cascade). Resolve the queued tags to a TargetPath the way the Sessions panel does (src/panel.rs).
- Empty queue: no-op plus a short info toast ("no agent needs you").
- New `Command` variant in src/keymap.rs (global section) with a default leader binding that does not collide with existing defaults; add it to Help. Follow .claude/skills/foreman-config-and-flags/SKILL.md for bindings.

OUT OF SCOPE: taskbar flash, fleet overview, any per-pane timestamp.

DONE WHEN:
- Pure, table-tested queue logic (push/dedupe/remove-on-leave/lazy-skip), separate from egui.
- A wm test: two panes in two projects enter NeedsYou in order A then B; the command surfaces A; after A gets PostToolUse it surfaces B; a closed pane is skipped.
- Grok (no PermissionRequest) simply never enters the queue; documented as a gotcha.
- docs/agent-state.md gains a short "Jump to next needs-you" section (what, binding, the queue rules above, gotchas); remove "jump to next needs-you" from the open list in docs/HANDOFF.md section 5 item 2.
- cargo build --target-dir target/agent adds no new warnings in touched files.

Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent agent_state then cargo test --target-dir target/agent (the integration queue runs the full suite per .foreman/integrate.json).
